paper_title: What Does Neuro Mean to Cardio Investigating the Role of Clinical   Specialty Data in Medical LLMs
caption_used: Negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between baseline MistralV0.2-Base and the same model further fine-tuned on each specialty data. The chart displays six specialty groups along the x-axis (Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, Pediatrics), with the y-axis showing negative log probability ranging from approximately -27 to -22. Within each group, the MistralV0.2-Base bar (light blue) consistently shows the highest negative log probability, indicating weaker token predictions at baseline. Among the fine-tuned models, the Gastro-tuned variant achieves the lowest negative log probability across most specialty groups, suggesting strong cross-specialty transfer. Notably, the Infect group shows the largest overall bar heights, with baseline reaching approximately -23.5, while the Cardio group exhibits the smallest spread between baseline and fine-tuned variants at roughly 1.5 units.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the negative log probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between the baseline MistralV0.2-Base model and the same model fine-tuned on different specialty data. The x-axis represents six medical specialty categories (Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics), while the y-axis displays the negative log probability, ranging from -27 to -22 on a linear scale with a tick label interval of 1. Within each specialty category, a group of bars is presented, with the light blue bar representing the MistralV0.2-Base model and the subsequent bars representing the model fine-tuned on different specialty data, colored according to the legend (Cardio: light orange, Gastro: peach, Infect: light brown, Neuro: brown, Obstetrics: dark brown, Pediatrics: dark orange). The bars are grouped by specialty category, with the MistralV0.2-Base bar consistently being the longest, having values ranging from approximately -26.5 for Cardio to -23.5 for Infect, while the fine-tuned bars are shorter, with varying lengths across specialty categories; for example, in the Cardio category, the fine-tuned bars range from approximately -22.5 to -23. The bars are not sorted in a specific order within each group, and no bars are visually emphasized. Overall, the chart displays a consistent pattern across the different specialty categories, with the baseline model showing the highest negative log probability and the fine-tuned models showing lower values.
